sources.title: Rosa Parks with Jim Haskins, Rosa Parks: My Story (1992)
National Women's History Museum -- Biography: Rosa Parks

risk_tolerance.rationale: Refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger in segregated Montgomery, Alabama in 1955, resulting in her arrest, a specific, extensively documented act carrying real, realized personal legal and social risk.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained direct confrontation with the segregated bus system and the resulting public and legal consequences of her arrest, documented via the well-established account of the incident and its aftermath, including job loss and death threats that followed.

discipline.rationale: Served for over a decade as secretary of the Montgomery NAACP chapter before her 1955 arrest, sustained documented civil-rights organizing work well before the bus incident that made her nationally known, per her own autobiography.

persistence.rationale: Continued civil-rights activism for decades after 1955, including co-founding the Rosa and Raymond Parks Institute for Self Development in 1987, documented via the well-established extended timeline of her later activism.

impact_motivation.rationale: Sustained decades of civil-rights organizing work both before and after the 1955 arrest that made her nationally known, documented via her own autobiography's account of her long involvement with the NAACP.

proactive_agency.rationale: Her own autobiography documents that her refusal was a considered decision in the moment rather than physical exhaustion (the popularized 'tired feet' narrative), stating she was 'tired of giving in' — a specific, directly self-documented account of deliberate action.

autonomy_need.rationale: Undertaking sensitive, personally dangerous investigative work (the Recy Taylor case) in the Jim Crow South as an individual NAACP representative required real personal self-direction, though the surviving record documents the investigation's occurrence more thoroughly than her specific individual working style within it.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained a decades-long commitment to civil-rights organizing work, both in a formal secretarial/organizational capacity and later through her own institute, suggesting real sustained purpose beyond the single well-known incident.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Served in an organizational, behind-the-scenes secretarial role for the Montgomery NAACP for years before the 1955 incident, suggesting a genuinely more understated, less publicly assertive working style than the historical prominence she later gained, distinct from more overtly public-speaking-oriented contemporaries.

collaboration.rationale: Served for fourteen years (1943-1957) as secretary to NAACP Montgomery chapter president E.D. Nixon and as the chapter's youth leader, sustained institutional civil-rights work within an organization well before the 1955 bus incident, documented in her own autobiography (Rosa Parks: My Story, 1992) and NAACP records.

detail_orientation.rationale: Personally conducted the NAACP's investigation into the gang rape of Recy Taylor in 1944, a specific, documented fact-finding investigation into a violent crime (extensively covered in civil-rights historiography, e.g. Danielle McGuire's At the Dark End of the Street), distinct from her later, better-known activism.

leadership_drive.rationale: Served as youth leader of the NAACP Montgomery chapter for over a decade before the bus boycott, a specific, documented role directly leading younger organizers, distinct from and prior to the fame that followed her own 1955 arrest.

independent_thinking.rationale: Her considered refusal to comply with segregation on that specific day, distinct from a spontaneous emotional reaction, reflects a real independent judgment against the era's dominant social norm, documented via her own autobiographical account.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Her documented fourteen-year progression from general NAACP membership to chapter secretary and youth leader suggests sustained development of organizational/institutional skill over time, though this is an inference from role progression rather than a single squarely on-point documented instance.

adaptability.rationale: Continued her activism after relocating from Montgomery to Detroit following the loss of employment and continued threats, adjusting her platform and approach across this major life disruption.

resourcefulness.rationale: Rebuilt her career and continued activism in Detroit after losing her Montgomery employment and facing sustained threats, suggesting real capacity to continue under significant material and personal disruption.

curiosity.rationale: Her sustained, decades-long engagement with organizing work across changing civil-rights strategies and later self-development education work suggests some real ongoing interest beyond a single fixed role.

planning_orientation.rationale: Her sustained NAACP secretarial work over a decade required organizing meetings, records, and case documentation, evidencing real administrative planning capacity ahead of the 1955 incident.

deep_focus.rationale: Her sustained secretarial and organizational NAACP work over a decade required real concentrated administrative attention.

systems_abstraction.rationale: Her later work founding an institute for structured self-development education suggests some real capacity for organizing a coherent programmatic framework.

provenance.notes: Third-batch diversity pick: 20th_century, north_america, civil-rights domain — deliberately distinct profile shape from the existing roster's civil-rights figures (Martin Luther King Jr., Frederick Douglass, Sojourner Truth, Malcolm X): a quieter, more procedural/organizational form of courage documented via her own autobiography's explicit correction of the popularized 'tired feet' narrative in favor of a considered, deliberate decision. UPDATE (session 6 diagnostic control experiment, 2026-08): received a genuine deep-research pass (her own 1992 autobiography Rosa Parks: My Story, and National Women's History Museum institutional source, documenting 14 years of pre-1955 NAACP institutional civil-rights work) distinct from and independent of the original batch-3 pass -- avgConf rose 0.479 -> 0.524, a real +0.045 gain, via 5 evidence-based upgrades (collaboration, leadership_drive, detail_orientation, autonomy_need, mastery_orientation). Still held: avgConf 0.524 remains meaningfully below the 0.55 floor even after this genuine deep pass -- unlike Kafka (0.001 short), this is a real, honest evidentiary gap, not a rounding-level miss. The available public record of her pre-1955 institutional work, while real and well documented in aggregate civil-rights historiography, does not map cleanly onto many of this taxonomy's 34 specific psychological-trait dimensions without straying into inference -- a genuine evidence-availability constraint, not a research-effort shortfall this session.

holdReason: Confidence ceiling after two remediation rounds (genuine evidence additions targeting missing high-baseWeight attributes, then a rubric-floor correction bringing every row already tagged evidenceType "documented" up to scoring-rubric-v1's own 0.65 floor for that tier -- never touching strong_inference/inference rows, never adding fabricated evidence): avgConf 0.479 vs 0.55 floor. This batch's research relied more heavily on general encyclopedic knowledge across many unfamiliar eras/regions/domains than a deeper per-person primary-source pass would support, and honestly lands at a lower average confidence tier than batches 1-2. A third confidence-adjustment round was deliberately NOT attempted -- per the session's own explicit instruction not to force wider margins or repeatedly rework a candidate just to cross the floor. A future session doing deeper per-person primary-source research could plausibly convert several of these (especially the ones within 0.02-0.04 of the floor) to accepted without inventing anything new.
